facts.claim: Startup path: reset 0x60080001 runs MPU and cache setup and scatter, then ITCM. Task inittsk starts at 0x1103D (record at 0x1FA74) and goes 0x1103C, 0x11698, 0x101E2, 0x80000B08. The small COPY row at 0x8383A30C, 0x118 bytes, is a list of 70 function pointers called in order at 0x80000B3C during start. Older notes called it a small data block.

facts.claim: Task attribute bit 0x1000 marks floating point tasks. facts.claim: Block render 0x1C2D0-0x1CA74: clears mix buffer 0x202AD3A0 (0xE00 bytes). For 32 voice slots, 0x58 bytes each from 0x202AE1A0, it calls voice render at 0x1C71E. The loop itself runs from ITCM, so that code does not depend on the cache.

Voice call: 0x1C71E does bl 0x1008E with r0 = voice slot, r1 = mix buffer, r2 and r3 = pointers to two out values on the stack. 0x1008E is a veneer to 0x80005870, which loads the state pointer from the slot, returns if empty, else jumps by veneer 0x800D2D5C to 0x14B88, the real voice renderer in ITCM. 0x1C71E is the only direct caller of 0x1008E, and the path crosses into SDRAM and back on every voice.

The voice state structure, sample engine, envelope, looper and resampler, the alternate flag and BUS routing have not been documented. Fields are known only in scattered reads, and the stand uses synthetic voices with no pitch, loop or reverse.

facts.claim: Project folder: B:/ROLAND/SP-404MKII/PROJECT_xx, xx 01-16. Contents: PADCONF.BIN (settings and pads), SMPL/BANK%d-%02d.SMP (samples; .WAV and .AIF also accepted by the name builder), PTN/PTN%05d.BIN (patterns), PTN/PATTERNCHAIN_%02d.CHN (chains), PICTURE/startup_1.bmp, startup_2.bmp, screen_saver_*.bmp. Empty slots do not need files. Also on B: _BackSamplingRec.bin, _emphasis.bin, FCTRY/FACTORY.SVD; on A: IMPORT, EXPORT, BKUP, update files in the root.

PADCONF.BIN: SAVE 0x800CF218 opens it with flags 0x601 at 0x800CF69E. LOAD 0x8018AE68 accepts only sizes 0x7B00, 0xCB00 and 0xCB20 (checks at 0x8018B156-0x8018B1E8). Pad records are 0xAC bytes, 160 of them (loop to 0x6B80). SAVE zeroes +0x68 to +0xAB of each at 0x800CF522-0x800CF532. So no free field survives and the file cannot grow. Layout (st.storage.formats): 'RFPD' at 0, 0xA0 at 4 (offset of the pad records), the version at 8 (3, or 2 in files from older firmware), 0x7A80 at 0xC, 28 words of project settings at 0x10, the project name (32 bytes) at 0x80, the 160 pad records of 0xAC bytes (43 big-endian words) from 0xA0, pad names (160 x 24 bytes) at 0x6C20, and per pad 0x80 bytes at 0x7B20 + pad x 0x80: the 16 marks, then 16 more words (st.chop.marks). 52000 bytes (0xCB20) is version 3 and 31488 (0x7B00) version 2, which has no name and no marks; the third size LOAD accepts, 0xCB00 (51968), is not described by SparkyMK2 and its origin is not known. Two sources agree on the zeroed tail: SparkyMK2 saw pad fields 27, 29 and 33 read 9000, 1 and 100 live over USB but 0 in the file, and in all 2080 pad records of 13 projects the owner's unit exported, bytes +0x68 to +0xAB were zero, as the SAVE code above writes them. The file can lag what the unit holds: SparkyMK2 found a deleted pad's old name and marks still in it.

facts.claim: A sample file BANKb-pp.SMP (b 1-10 for banks A-J, pp 01-16) is a 512-byte header and 16-bit signed big-endian PCM, channels interleaved. facts.claim: A pattern file PTN/PTNnnnnn.BIN (nnnnn = pattern index + 1, A1 = 00001) is a run of 8-byte records ending with an end record (type 0x8C in byte 1) and an 8-byte trailer. Byte 0 of each record is the ticks to the next record, at 480 ticks a quarter note; byte 1 is the type: 0x2F-0x7F a note on a pad (0x2F + bank within its group x 16 + pad - 1, the group, A-E or F-J, in the low nibble of byte 2), 0x8E a controller change, other values from 0x80 only advance time (FF 80 00 ... fills gaps over 255 ticks); bytes 4 and 5 are note-on and note-off velocity and 6-7 the gate length in ticks, little-endian. In the trailer byte 4 is the time signature. Byte 0 of the trailer is the length in bars: SparkyMK2 only saw 4 (7680 ticks) and called that a guess; in the 4 patterns the owner's unit exported it was 2 and each ran 3840 ticks, 2 bars of 4/4. PTN/PATTERNCHAIN_00.CHN is a small XML file listing the chain's patterns by number.

facts.claim: Waveform of the marker screen. 0x800552F0 is not a background job, as this entry said before: it creates the marker screen object (new of 0x570 bytes through 0x800D8B14, vtable 0x80227008, st.chop.marker-screen), reached through 0x800BDA40 (handle kept at screen + 0x1A6C). Two peak buffers, 0x82E0D748 and 0x82E0DEA0 (vtable 0x8022D234), each hold from +4 127 pairs of 16-bit numbers, one per screen column; +0x200 = 0x000F0001, +0x204 pad (bank x 16 + number, 16 bits; 0x800D0908 splits it), +0x206 zoom power, +0x208 step (frames per column), +0x20C length in frames = (bytes - 0x200) / 4, +0x210 current column, +0x21C window start, +0x224 ready flag. Which half of a pair is the maximum is written both ways in the source notes; the reset fills each pair with 0x7FFF in the first halfword and 0x8000 in the second, so treat the order as not settled. Reset 0x800BF858(buffer) also sets step = max(1, length / 127 >> zoom). Update 0x80194128(buffer), reached from 0x800A4630, asks the peak cache 0x82E024D8 for each column through 0x80100A38(cache, pair, ..., position, step); 0x80100C40 looks up a block in a linked list by a five-word key and creates it when missing (new of 0x770 bytes, holding a reader object with vtable 0x8021D068). 0x800C1AE0(0x82E024D8) returns all cache blocks (up to 516) to the malloc pool; the stock calls it when the pad changes and on leaving the screen. On entering the screen the columns are written by 0x801941B6 in the screen's own flow: 0x80073B76 -> 0x8014B4F0 -> 0x800A4630 -> 0x80100A38. facts.claim: Cutting a pad into chops: 0x80047EB0, reached by a tail branch at 0x8005CA42 (path 0x8004F498 -> 0x8005CA28 -> 0x80047EB0, run in PANEL TASK from the button handler, on the same stack as key events), builds a job on its stack (+0 bank, +4 pad, the AUTO MARK values as in st.chop.automark, +0x1C 16 mark positions, +0x5C 16 assigned pads, read by unrolled runs of parameters 0xA2 and 0xA6). Stock order: 0x800CF878(0x82E46658), 0x800CEC38(0x82E46610), then 0x800AE700(0x80591800, pad, 0xA0, 0, 0), which copies the source pad to the temporary pad 160, so the job names bank 10, pad 0 (the copy), not the source; then the chop executor 0x8017C828 (the firmware's own strings name it ExeChop) with the object 0x80B499EC and the job, from 0x800480F8; then 0x800D08E0(0x80591800, 0xA0) and 0x800CE498(0xA0) remove the copy, then 0x800C0A80(0x80591800, 7, pad, 0), 0x800D9F58(0x80249734, project) and 0x800CFE18(0x82E46610). ExeChop counts the marks that are not -1 and skips a mark whose pad is -1. Per chop, 0x8017AC88 takes start = job + 0x1C + 4i and end = job + 0x20 + 4i; the last chop (i = count - 1, count at chopper + 0x2000) ends at the source pad's parameter 0x66, the sample end, read with 0x800D9EB8 (0x8017ACC4-0x8017ACD2). Each chop becomes its own SMP file and an ordinary pad record. The executor loops exactly 16 times (0x8017C976: cmp r6,#16). It returns 0, -113 (no marks) or -127 (a chop failed). On the emulator every chop but the last came out one frame longer than the gap between its marks (sample record length 0x200 + 4 x frames): that is how the stock cuts. Calling ExeChop once per chop (marks i and i+1 only, the last with one mark) gave byte for byte the same chops as one call of 15. Because the work runs inside PANEL TASK, the screen does not change while it cuts (st.ui.commit). None of this was measured separately on a unit.

facts.claim: AUTO MARK analysis: 0x8017B410(0x80B499EC, job), the object being the chopper (CChop). The stock AUTO MARK screen builds the job at 0x80048198 after calling 0x8010E980(project). Job words: 0 bank (0-9; 10 is the temporary pad 160), 1 pad 0-15, 2 mode (project value 0x9D), 3 LEVEL 1-10 (0x9F), 4 the value 0xA1 (meaning not found), 5 TIME DIVISION (0x9E), 6 TRANSIENT 0 HARD, 1 MID, 2 SOFT (0xA0), 7-22 (+0x1C) the answer: up to 16 marks in frames, -1 for unused, 23-38 (+0x5C) the pad of each mark, used when cutting (st.chop.job). A tbb at 0x8017B424 switches on word 2: 0 TIME DIVISION, done in the dispatcher itself; 1 LEVEL 0x8017BC48 (st.chop.automark-level); 2 TRANSIENT 0x8017C138 (st.chop.automark-transient); 4 0x8017B920, equal parts from project value 0x6F and a table of 10 words (perhaps division by tempo: a guess); 3 nothing. The analysis reads some of its settings from the project values, not from the job, so 0x9D, 0x9F, 0xA0 and 0x9E must be set before the call: without them TRANSIENT found nothing on the emulator. The return value is not a count: TRANSIENT returns -127 (0xFFFFFF81) even when it found marks, and the stock screen does not look at it; read the job instead. The analysis always runs from the first frame of the sample file to the pad's end point (0x66); the pad's start point (0xAB) is ignored, so a copy of a pad with its start in the middle gave the marks of the first half, and analysing a sample in halves this way does not work. The limit is 16 marks counting the start (mark 0). Sound is read through 0x800D9158(0x82F5C760, pad, -1) for the sample record (+0xC the channel count), 0x800D9000(0x82F5C760, record, byte offset) for a cache block, offset = frame x 2 x channels + 0x200 for the header, and 0x800D3090 for each 16-bit sample. TIME DIVISION splits the length into 2-16 equal parts, step = length / N; how the remainder is spread (perhaps one frame to each of the first parts) is not decoded. facts.claim: AUTO MARK TRANSIENT is one float function, 0x8017C138-0x8017C768 (about 1.6 KB). Its threshold is a double from the table 0x801E4FD8 at index 0, 6 or 12 for HARD, MID or SOFT, turned into a float. It reads the sound in blocks of 1024 frames, the left channel as floats into the chopper object at +0 and the right one (when project value 0x65 is 2, stereo) at +0x1000, each sample divided by 32768. For each frame it compares with the previous sample (a product below 0 is a sign change), keeps envelopes of the magnitude, and takes a candidate when the current peak exceeds the previous one times the threshold. Marks are at least 2400 frames apart (cmp with 0x960 at 0x8017C4AA and 0x8017C5EA; 0x95E and 0x95F are used to pull a mark to a zero crossing); when a new mark is nearer than 2400 frames to the last one, the smaller position of the two stays. The list is 16 words at 0x830089E0, filled with -1 first; the count is a register (sb) and the stop is 'more than 15', cmp.w sb,#0xf at 0x8017C368 and 0x8017C500. At the end it closes the cache file (0x800DEBD8), clears fields of 0x82F5C760 and copies the 16 words into the job at +0x1C. On the emulator, pad B-16: HARD reached the limit of 16 with all marks in the first quarter of the sample (2731, 7767, 14882, ... 107410), MID gave 8, SOFT none besides the start. facts.claim: The marker screen (page 8, st.chop.screens) is an object with vtable 0x80227008, created by 0x800552F0 (st.chop.waveform). Fields: +0x3F0 cursor column, +0x3F8 end, +0x3FC cursor, +0x474 = 1, +0x4D8 frames per column, +0x4E4 window start, +0x500 window for the cursor, +0x504 + 4i the window for mark i, +0x544 ZOOM 0-9, +0x550 what was touched last (1 cursor, 2 mark). Frames per column = (end / 127) >> ZOOM, plus 1 at 1x when 127 columns do not reach the end (0x8014D76C). The window at a ZOOM = clamp(centre - 63 columns, 0, end - 127 columns), the centre being the cursor or the selected mark; on B-16 this gave 73440 at z5, 79677 at z6 and 85536 at z10, as the stock showed. The window of each mark is kept per mark and equals mark - 63 columns: pressing the mark's pad or choosing it with CTRL3 puts the mark in the middle of the screen (on B-16 at ZOOM 6x, pads 1-5 gave windows 0, 54221, 156045, 257869, 337419); MARK does not move the window, since the new mark is under the cursor already. The knobs are absolute, value 0-127 being a column: CTRL1 puts the cursor at window + value x step; CTRL3 selects mark (value x N + 64) / 128 of N; CTRL2 takes hold of the selected mark (flag at screen + 0xA6) only when the knob comes within 2 columns of it (vtable + 4, for marks 0x8014B610: (mark - window) / step) and then puts the mark in the knob's column (vtable + 8), so the mark follows the knob across the window and ZOOM gives the precision (0x8014CC38-0x8014CC6A). facts.claim: Stock message boxes are opened with 0x800D8C88(0x82DFD314, id, own text or 0). Their table is at 0x801F7A90, 40 bytes per id: +0 the kind, +0x10 a pointer to the text. Kind 9 is a message that goes away by itself; kind 2 has CANCEL and OK. Ids around CHOP: 17 No Sample Selected, 19 Cannot Move Start Mark, 20 Cannot Add Mark, 21 Cannot Add Mark Too Close, 22 Cannot Delete Start Mark, 23 and 24 Current Marks will be lost, 25 Current Assign will be lost, 26 No Mark Present, 27 Not All Marks Assigned!, 28 No Assign!, 29 Attention! No Empty Pad for Assign, 30 Attention! alone. Given its own text, the function copies it with malloc to +0x184 of the box object. How a caller learns whether OK or CANCEL was chosen on kind 2 is not established.
